newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen reports progress on French hostage talks.
newsitem.headline: Yemen reports progress on French hostage talks.

text.p: Yemen said on Thursday it was making progress in negotiations with the kidnappers of a French diplomat and hoped for an imminent breakthrough.

"There is positive progress (in negotiations)...Which does not make us think of using force," Abdul-Wali al-Shumairi, governor of Marib province, told Reuters. "We expect a breakthrough within the next 12 hours."
The diplomat was kidnapped in Sanaa on Monday by members of the al-Toaiman tribe and is being held in Marib, 170 km (100 miles) northeast of Sanaa.

Shumairi said mediators from other tribes, negotiating on behalf of the government, had asked for more time due to the "positive progress" which prompted authorities to extend indefinitely a Wednesday night deadline to attack the kidnappers if they did not release the diplomat.
He would not say what kind of progress has been made.
He said French ambassador Marcel Laugel has been in Marib since Wednesday. Shumairi had said the kidnappers wanted to "open dialogue" with the French embassy.

The tribe is seeking government compensation for losses inflicted on homes, farms, water pumps and wells by floods that killed 65 people in June. It also wants more job opportunities and the settlement of a land dispute.
French embassy officials have refused to give details on the diplomat, who Yemeni authorities say is a first secretary at the embassy.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners for use as bargaining chips.
At least two diplomats, an American and a Saudi ambassador, have been among the kidnap victims.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
